idiom_name: duck typing; protocol by member presence (Symbol.iterator and friends)
implementation_notes: JavaScript has no static types to erase: any object can be stored in any variable, and behaviour is selected by member lookup at call time, so 'one interface holding unrelated types' is just a property or an argument that gets called. The language's well-known protocols are structural: an object becomes iterable by carrying Symbol.iterator, a thenable by carrying then - for...of, spread and await bind to any object with the right members regardless of constructor or prototype chain. Where a named contract is wanted for people and tooling, declare the shape in JSDoc/TypeScript and check the members at the boundary; for a closed set of shapes, an explicit tag/discriminated union restores the exhaustiveness the dynamic protocol cannot provide.
pitfalls: No runtime enforcement: a misspelled method surfaces as a TypeError at the call site (or a silently skipped optional callback), so validate untrusted values at the boundary.
Method extraction loses the receiver: passing obj.draw as a callback leaves this undefined in strict mode - wrap it in an arrow function or bind it.
Patching prototypes or relying on Symbol-key collisions changes behaviour process-wide and makes the implicit contract invisible; prefer per-object protocol members or adapters.
